title: fleet repository row
description: One line of repos.jsonl written by skills/fleet/scripts/fleet.py. A failed row has a reason token and null signals_schema_version, scans, active, head_sha, dirty and dirty_reason. An ok row's active says whether its HEAD was committed inside the run's window; head_sha is the HEAD it measured and dirty says whether tracked files differed from it, in which case HEAD's committed tree was scanned (untracked files, .assess/ outputs and a submodule's own edits never count). dirty is null on an ok row only when the state is unknown, and dirty_reason then says why: no_commit (scanned in place), status_error, index_read_error, sparse_checkout, skip_worktree or assume_unchanged (git status never compares those entries); with a HEAD, an unknown state is scanned from the committed tree like a dirty one. A clean row's dirty_reason is submodule_dirty when a submodule held uncommitted tracked edits: the checkout was scanned in place, those edits included. Generated from lib/fleet/runner.py by lib/fleet/fleet_schema.py.

reason.description: 'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: shallow_clone (the checkout is a shallow clone, so a reverting or rewriting commit may be cut from the history read); shallow_unknown (git could not confirm the checkout is a full clone); not_a_repo (the path is not a git repository, or one with no commits); no_git (git is not installed where the scan ran); git_failed (a git read past the windowed log (a patch-id, numstat or blame read) failed on a repository the log could read); git_timeout (a git read took longer than the scan allows). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

agent_outcome.description: Revert and rework rate of the agent commits of the run window (lib/agent_outcome.py, issue #1085). Informational: no Step, count or headline reads it. Reverted: a later commit's 'This reverts commit' message names it, or a later commit's diff is its exact inverse (equal git patch-id). Reworked: git blame, rework_days after the commit, no longer attributes some line it added to it. A share with nothing to divide by is null with a token reason.

ci_checks.description: Does CI run a test or lint check (lib/ci/ci_checks.py), read from the git-tracked CI files and the GitLab includes resolved offline (lib/ci/ci_includes.py: local files, and project or component files of clones in the --ghsync-root). test_or_lint_configured is true when an own or included CI line runs one, false when none does and every include resolved, and null (unknown) when a CI file pulls jobs from a file this run could not read (an unresolved GitLab include, a reusable workflow in another repository); basis says which. Under --platform, a repository with an unresolved GitLab include also gets GitLab's merged configuration from the CI lint API (lib/hosting/gitlab_ci_lint.py), counted apart in merged_check_commands; a template resolved offline wins. enforced_check_runs (issue #775) is the same test with masked checks left out (|| true, continue-on-error: true, allow_failure: true, set +e without a re-raise; lib/ci/ci_masking.py) and checks off the ordinary triggers left out (lib/ci/ci_triggers.py); masked_check_commands and off_trigger_check_commands count the lines left out. lint_runs (issue #782) is the enforced test for lint lines only (Layer 3 level 1); a check target or script that may run a linter inside it reads null. CI files of other systems are not parsed (issues #787, #928): unread_ci_files counts them, and with no readable check one makes basis unread_ci_system and enforced_check_runs null (and lint_runs null with no readable lint line). The unread-CI paths, all relative to the repository root: Jenkinsfile, .circleci/config.yml, bitbucket-pipelines.yml, .travis.yml, azure-pipelines.yml, azure-pipelines.yaml, .azure-pipelines.yml, .azure-pipelines.yaml, .buildkite/pipeline.yml, .buildkite/pipeline.yaml, buildkite.yml, buildkite.yaml, .ci.yaml (Flutter Cocoon / LUCI), .prow.yaml, .zuul.yaml, .drone.yml, .woodpecker.yml, .cirrus.yml, appveyor.yml, .semaphore/semaphore.yml, cloudbuild.yaml, bitrise.yml and codemagic.yaml; any *.star or *.cfg file under infra/config/ (LUCI project configuration); any *.yml or *.yaml file under .azure/pipelines/, eng/pipelines/, .azure-pipelines/, azure-pipelines/ (Azure Pipelines) or .woodpecker/; and any file under zuul.d/ (lib/unread_ci.py). Off-repository CI (issue #928): under --platform, when more than half of the sampled merged pull requests carry a check run or commit status of a known external CI system (lib/external_ci.py, at most two GET calls per sampled pull request), the false cases read null with basis external_ci; offline, a root Prow OWNERS_ALIASES file with no CI file of any kind reads null with basis external_ci_marker. Neither earns credit.

kind.description: local, project, component, template, remote, or unknown (an include entry this reader cannot parse; status unparsed).

id.description: gitlab_project:<path> or gitlab_component:<path>; null for the other kinds.

status.description: resolved; toolkit_gate (the toolkit's own regression gate template, known to run no project tests); or why not: no_root, not_cloned, file_missing, not_offline (template, remote), glob, bad_path, depth_limit, file_limit, unparsed, ref_missing (a pin the clone does not hold).

ref_basis.description: How the file was read: at the pinned ref, at the clone's HEAD (no pin), or from the work tree; null when not resolved.

depth.description: Include level: 1 for the repository's own include.

rename.description: A project or component with no clone at its written path (#1357): followed (read from the clone at the path GitLab's API answered under), checked (looked up, no clone at a new path) or not_checked (offline, or not answered); null for every other include.

includes.description: One record per include item, nested includes after their parent; no file name or text.

merged_config.description: The CI lint API read: not_read (offline), not_needed (every include resolved offline), read, invalid (GitLab marked the configuration invalid) or unavailable.

merged_config_reason.description: The reason code when merged_config is unavailable (no_access, not_found, not_gitlab, ...); null otherwise.

merged_check_commands.description: Lines of the merged configuration that run a test or lint check; the text is never published.

test_or_lint_configured.description: The CI test-or-lint signal: true, false, or null when included jobs may hold the check or a Maven run skips its tests.

basis.description: The reason for test_or_lint_configured: check_command or merged_config (true; the second when only the merged configuration ran a check), included_jobs or merged_config_partial (null; the second when the merged configuration was read with no check but may lack jobs: an include under rules:, or a trigger: child pipeline), check_target (null: no check, but a Maven or Gradle run with its tests skipped, mvn -DskipTests verify or ./gradlew check -x test, which may still run a lint task), unread_ci_system (false: no readable check, but a CI file of a system the scan does not parse is tracked), external_ci or external_ci_marker (false: no readable check, but CI runs off the repository; as enforced_basis), no_check_command or no_ci (false).

enforced_check_runs.description: Layer 5 level 1: true when a CI line runs a check that can fail its job on ordinary changes, null when none does but included jobs, unsettled triggers, a committed script the tree does not hold, a target whose recipe is not read, a CI system the scan does not parse or an external CI system may hold one, else false.

enforced_basis.description: The reason for enforced_check_runs: enforced_check (true), included_jobs, unknown_trigger, check_may_pass (a check whose failure the step may hide: pytest || echo failed, an if or while condition, an until loop that breaks out, a check before && with more of the step after it, a { } group or function called in such a position; issue #1008), script_not_found, check_target or unread_ci_system (null), external_ci (null: an external check context on merged changes under --platform; more than half of the sampled merged pull requests carry a check run or commit status of a known external CI system such as Buildkite, LUCI, Prow tide or Azure Pipelines, read with at most two GET calls per sampled pull request; it never gives credit), external_ci_marker (null: offline, a root Prow OWNERS_ALIASES file with no CI file present, neither a workflow, a .gitlab-ci.yml nor an unread CI file; an OWNERS file alone is not a marker), not_enforced, no_check_command or no_ci (false).

masked_check_commands.description: CI lines that run a check whose failure cannot fail the job.

off_trigger_check_commands.description: Unmasked CI check lines whose workflow or job does not run on ordinary changes (workflow_dispatch or schedule only, a manual GitLab job).

lint_runs.description: Layer 3 level 1 (issue #782): true when a CI line runs a linter that can fail its job on ordinary changes (not --version or --help), or a step uses a known lint action (golangci-lint-action, ruff-action, super-linter, reviewdog) not set to install only (issue #893: ruff-action args --version, golangci-lint-action install-only true), null when none does but included jobs, a reviewdog step with no failing fail_level (it cannot fail its job), unsettled triggers, a lint script the tree does not hold or a check target or script that may lint inside it could hold one, or when the only static gate is a compiler run with warnings as errors or a .NET build's analysers (issue #926), else false. A formatter that rewrites files counts only when a later line of its job runs git diff --exit-code.

lint_basis.description: The reason for lint_runs: lint_command (true), included_jobs, merged_config_partial, unknown_trigger, check_may_pass, script_not_found, check_target, unread_ci_system, external_ci or external_ci_marker (null; as enforced_basis), analysers_in_build (null: a CI .NET build runs the analysers a committed Directory.Build.props or .csproj turns on with EnforceCodeStyleInBuild or AnalysisLevel; their severities live in .editorconfig, which the scan does not evaluate), compiler_gate_only (null: the only static gate is a compiler run with warnings as errors, such as mix compile --warnings-as-errors, -Werror or TreatWarningsAsErrors; issue #926), not_enforced, no_lint_command or no_ci (false).

unread_ci_files.description: Tracked CI files of systems the scan does not parse, at the unread-CI paths the block description lists; a count, never the paths.

reason.description: 'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: short_history (the window holds fewer than 10 first-parent commits, too few for a share to mean anything); shallow_clone (the checkout is a shallow clone, so the merges read are cut short); shallow_unknown (git could not confirm the checkout is a full clone); not_a_repo (the path is not a git repository, or one with no commits); no_git (git is not installed where the scan ran); git_failed (a git read after the first (the merge log or the attribute read) failed on a repository the first read could open); git_timeout (a git read took longer than the scan allows). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

concurrency.description: How often the same files change across merges (lib/history/concurrency.py, issue #985): the newest merge_sample first-parent commits of the run window, each file's share of them, the files at or above threshold, the median files per merge, the generated files touched (a linguist-generated attribute, a generated name or a generator header) and the registry fan-in of the files above threshold. Informational: no Step, count or headline reads it.

threshold.description: The touch share (0 to 1) a file is counted above at or past: 0.25, one merge in four.

files_above_threshold.description: Files whose touch share is at or above threshold.

max_touch_share.description: The highest touch share of any file.

generated_files_touched.description: Distinct generated files the merges changed.

generated_merge_share.description: Share (0 to 1) of merges that changed a generated file.

max_fan_in.description: Most distinct top-level folders changed beside one file above threshold; null when no file is above it.

hot_files.description: The files above threshold (at most 20) with their touch share, generated flag and fan-in; empty in counts-only output, where files_above_threshold carries the count.

coverage_gate.description: Committed line-coverage thresholds (lib/testing/coverage_gate.py), read from config and CI files at HEAD, never from measured coverage. Each gate keeps its threshold as written beside threshold_percent, the same value as a percentage (a JaCoCo ratio 0.80 is 80).

reason.description: Why the block is unavailable.

configured.description: True when any gate gates something (a non-zero threshold, or a null one from a tool default or a templated flag). Read from configuration text at HEAD; was enforced before issue #783. A root coverage.py gate listed on a scoped run whose hold on the scope is not resolved (unmeasured_reason root_coverage_config_unresolved, issue #1032) is not counted here.

threshold.description: The threshold as written; null when not read (a template variable, a tool default).

threshold_percent.description: The threshold as a percentage: as written for percent, times 100 for ratio; null for uncovered_count, missed_ratio (a JaCoCo MISSEDRATIO maximum) or a threshold not read.

gates.description: Each gate found, with its file and 1-based line.

max_threshold_percent.description: The highest non-null threshold_percent across the gates; null when no gate has one. An unresolved root gate on a scoped run (issue #1032) and a Codecov patch target (issue #882) are left out.

threshold_meets_minimum.description: The Layer 6 level 1 signal: true when a counted gate's threshold_percent is at least 50; null (unknown) when none is but a counted gate's percentage was not read, or when a repository holding a go.mod or Cargo.toml has no gate of that language and none of at least 50 for another, or when a Codecov project status target is auto or missing, or the only Codecov status is a patch status, and no other gate decides it (issue #882), or when a scoped run cannot tell whether the root coverage.py floor governs the scope and that floor would change the reading (see unmeasured_reason); false otherwise. Gates counted are those enforced counts.

unmeasured_reason.description: Why threshold_meets_minimum is null when no gate of the repository's Go or Rust module is found: go_rust_gate_form_not_read when the repository holds a go.mod or Cargo.toml with no gate read for it and none of at least 50 percent for another language (issue #937), so its gate may be a script this scan does not read; root_coverage_config_unresolved on a scoped run when the repository root's coverage.py floor would change the reading but where CI runs coverage is not resolved (issue #1032); codecov_target_not_read when the only gate that could reach 50 percent is a Codecov project status with an auto, missing or non-numeric target, codecov_patch_only when it is a Codecov patch status, which bounds changed lines only (issue #882); null otherwise.

enforced_meets_minimum.description: The Layer 6 level 1 signal (issue #921): threshold_meets_minimum with a CI run required. True when it is true and an enforced CI line (unmasked, on ordinary triggers; lib/ci/ci_masking.py, lib/ci/ci_triggers.py) passes a counted threshold of at least 50 itself or runs the tool that reads it; null when threshold_meets_minimum is null or the run cannot be told (see enforced_basis); false otherwise.

enforced_basis.description: The reason for enforced_meets_minimum: ci_run (true); no_gate, threshold_below_minimum, not_run_in_ci and no_ci (false); threshold_not_read, unknown_trigger, check_may_pass (the run's failure may not fail its job: pytest --cov || echo failed; issue #1008), indirect_run (a check target or script such as make test may run it), included_jobs, unread_ci_system and status_check_unconfirmed (a Codecov status target, which no CI line runs and which gates a merge only when branch protection requires it; issue #882) (null).

instruction_presence.description: root: a file at a root location (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, .cursorrules, .github/copilot-instructions.md and the others instruction_files grades) or one the tool loads at session start, always loaded. nested_only: no root file, but a nested or path-scoped file (pkg/AGENTS.md, a .claude/rules file with paths), loaded on demand where the agent works. stub: every root file holds only headings and blank lines, and no nested file exists (#922). none: no instruction file at any known location. Null when there is no root file with a body (none, or only stubs) and the nested_instructions scan did not run.

instruction_file_present.description: True for root and nested_only, false for stub and none, null with instruction_presence. Layer 0 level 1 of the default maturity model reads it.

instructions_grade.description: Best letter grade (A to F) of the files instruction_presence counts: the root files, else the always-loaded or nested ones, or a stub's. Null only for none.

reason.description: 'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: agent_workflows_unread (a workflow calls an unread reusable workflow in another repository whose path names an agent. Agent work: a scheduled or event-triggered caller, and no local agent workflow. Job scope: a caller on any trigger without a read-only scope, and no local agent job that settles it); no_agent_jobs (with agent_job_count at 0, no committed workflow job runs an agent, so there is no agent job scope to read); agent_job_scope_unread (an agent job's permissions could not be read. They may be an expression or an unknown value, or the agent sign sits outside every job. No other agent job settles the reading). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: no_pr_workflows (no GitHub Actions workflow runs on pull requests, so this reader sees no check that could read an AI disclosure. A bot or an app could still do it). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: form_unreadable (no issue form read has a required field, and a GitHub issue form could not be read. Causes are a tab indent, an unclosed flow collection, no top-level body list, or a file over the size limit); gitlab_template_unreadable (no form or template read meets the bar. A GitLab issue template could not be read: it is too large or could not be opened); gitlab_ci_unreadable (no workflow adds an untriaged label, and .gitlab-ci.yml has a tab in its indentation or an unclosed flow collection, which GitLab rejects); gitlab_ci_unsettled (no workflow or GitLab job read adds an untriaged label on a schedule. But something this reader cannot follow may: an include not read offline, or an anchor merge, !reference, variable label or unread rule); workflow_unreadable (no workflow read adds an untriaged label when an issue opens, and a workflow's on: key could not be read); stale_input_unresolved (no stale job is sure to close a ready issue. But one sets its close days or exempt labels to an expression, which this reader does not follow); no_network (the issue tracker was not read: a headless run without --platform, or the host could not be reached); no_platform_auth (the issue tracker could not be read: gh or glab is missing or signed out, or the token was refused the issues); unsupported_host (the repository has no remote, or its host is not GitHub or a GitLab that glab reaches, so its issues were not read); platform_error (a read of the issue tracker failed for a reason other than access, such as a rate limit or a server error); empty_window (the metric has nothing to measure yet: no issue in the window, none answered, or no open issue older than 7 days); response_unread (a first response may exist that was not read: a long timeline, the note cap or an unclassified account); window_truncated (the window's issue list passed the read cap, so issues may be missing. The ratio is not taken, nor the median when no issue read was answered); open_truncated (the open-issue list passed the read cap, so the untriaged share would cover only part of it and is not taken); response_pending (the median wait is not settled yet: issues still unanswered could put it either side of first_response_max_days, depending on when they are answered); no_response (no issue opened in the window got a first response from a person, and each has waited longer than first_response_max_days). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: no_pr_checks (no GitHub Actions workflow runs a test or lint command on pull requests. So this reader sees no check a label could skip); no_ci_files (the tree tracks no GitHub Actions workflow, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile or root pom.xml, so there is no build setting to read). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: no_model_jobs (with model_jobs at 0, no model-calling CI job was detected, so there is nothing to gate. A model call inside a script file a job runs is not read); trigger_unresolved (the ungated count is null and ungated_reason holds this code. No model-backed job is ungated, but one could not be settled. Examples are an unreadable on: key, a label if: joined with ||, or a job that only names a provider secret. A GitLab merge that is not settled reads the same way); eval_ci_unread (an agent eval suite holds a committed baseline, but no CI file that was read runs it. A CI file or GitLab include was not read, and it may run the suite); ci_jobs_unread (the ungated count is null and ungated_reason holds this code. Every model-backed job found is gated. But a job calls a reusable workflow from another repository on a route that is not gated, or a GitLab include was not read. An ungated job may sit there). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: knowledge_base (the repository is a knowledge base (archetype knowledge-base), which takes no code patches); org_policy_not_read (the repository holds no security policy. The owner's shared .github repository, whose policy GitHub shows on this one, was not read. The cause is offline use, no --platform, a remote not on github.com, or gh not signed in). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: ci_not_read (no CI check that keeps docs or generated files true was found. The tree tracks a CI file of a system this reader does not parse, such as Jenkins, Prow or Buildkite. Or .gitlab-ci.yml has an include: this reader does not follow. Either may run one); scan_failed (the reader of CI checks that keep docs true raised an error. The doc staleness block is kept, and this one condition reads not measured). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: settings_not_readable (only a repository admin, organization owner or security manager can read GitHub's secret scanning and push protection settings). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: no_remote (the repository has no github.com remote, so there is no owner .github repository to read). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: ci_not_read (no guard was found, and something here may run one that this reader cannot see. That is a CI file of a system it does not parse, or a .gitlab-ci.yml include: it does not follow. It can also be a step it could not settle, such as a remote reusable workflow); trigger_unknown (a guard was found only in a workflow or GitLab job whose trigger this reader could not settle. So it cannot say the guard runs on ordinary changes); no_guard_script (every guard found is a third-party tool or an architecture test with no committed script of its own. So there is no guard script whose tests to look for); scan_failed (the reader of ratchets and repo-owned guards raised an error, so both conditions read not measured). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: network (no AI review step is committed in CI, and a headless run without --platform makes no GitHub or GitLab read); no_remote (no AI review step is committed in CI and the repository has no GitHub or GitLab remote, so there are no merged changes to read). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: secret_scanning_not_read (no secrets scan runs in CI, and the repository is on GitHub, whose own secret scanning and push protection were not read); gitlab_rules_unevaluated (a GitLab job holds a secrets scan but runs under rules, only/except or a when that is not evaluated. Or its merged definitions could not be settled. So it is not known whether the scan runs on each change); ci_includes_unresolved (no secrets scan was found in the CI read. A GitLab include that could hold one, a local, project or remote file, was not read). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: skill_files_unread (a skill or agent file could not be read, and none of those read holds a detected kind). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: no_grimp (grimp, the Python import-graph builder, is not installed); no_networkx (networkx, which the structure metrics need, is not installed); grimp_failed (grimp could not build the Python import graph); no_python_packages (a Python repository with no importable package); no_builder:<language> (no import graph builder covers the dominant source language, for example no_builder:java; no other language's graph stands in, and the sentence names a tool that would build one where one is known, jdeps for the JVM languages); no_import_graph_<language> (a builder covers the dominant source language but found nothing to graph in it, for example no_import_graph_go); invalid_import_graph (a builder returned a graph that breaks the module-graph contract); no_source_files (the scope holds no source file in a language the assess skill recognises). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: no_ownership_map (the repository commits no ownership or boundary map (CODEOWNERS, an ARCHITECTURE module list) for the drift check to read). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

pack.description: Present only with --pack (lib/pack_checks.py): {<pack>: {<check>: value}}, read at pack.<pack>.<check>. A value is a boolean (exists, key_exists), a file count (glob_count, contains) or {available: false} when the check could not be answered; never a path or file text.
